clue.text: Jam jar jar?

parts.note: jam jar is rhyming slang for a car, so a car jar is the jolt to the neck suffered in a collision

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a jar of jam being shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: 'jam jar' rhymes with 'car', so a 'jam jar jar' is a jarring of the car, as in a rear-end shunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck injury caused by a sudden jolt, typically in a car crash, which is exactly a car being jarred.

clue.text: Type of gun with catches raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down, so it is read bottom to top

parts.note: nets means catches, as a fisherman does

explanation.surface: A firearm described as one that has its safety catches lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sten was a British submachine gun of the Second World War, so it is a type of gun.

clue.text: Article on scuba divers, one reckons

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: divers is an old word for various or different, so the letters of scuba are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A magazine article about scuba divers and someone who weighs things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' looks like the people in wetsuits; here it is the old adjective meaning 'various', the anagram signal. In a down clue 'on' puts the article above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads used for counting, so it is a thing that reckons or calculates.

clue.text: Tool isn't blue, not black variety

indicators.note: not says the letter for black is to be left out of the letters available
variety asks for a different arrangement of the remaining letters

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone insisting a tool is not a blue thing, nor a black variety.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of ISN'T BLUE, remove B (black, signalled by 'not'), and rearrange the rest as 'variety' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is an implement or tool, especially one used in the kitchen.

clue.text: Build-up of massive temperature under home essential

indicators.note: in a down clue the temperature letter sits under the word for home

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: in a down clue, building a word up reads it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: large means massive

explanation.surface: Weather talk about a big rise in temperature beneath one's house being vital.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Build-up of' reads the synonym upwards, and 'under' sets the temperature letter beneath the word for home.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral means necessary to make a whole complete, which is a synonym of essential.

clue.text: "Oh, feels so good", sent shivers down one's spine

indicators.note: sent here means sent flying or sent into disorder, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming in pleasure while a thrill runs down their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent' is the anagram signal, as in sent flying; G for good comes first, although 'good' sits inside the quotation in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumps on the skin raised by cold or fear, accompanying the tingling feeling of a chill up and down the back.

clue.text: Scrounge one and sling your hook

parts.note: beg means scrounge or cadge

explanation.surface: Someone told to take one handout and clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sling your hook' is British slang for 'go away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an old command to leave at once, matching the slang order to clear off.

clue.text: See 25
I won't be gone long? Ultimate in patience this to hang on?

parts.note: the phrase someone leaves on a note, back soon, read cryptically as the word soon written back to front

indicators.note: ultimate in means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone promising a quick return, while another runs out of patience and contemplates the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I won't be gone long' is 'back soon', which cryptically says SOON backwards, NOOS; add E, the last letter of 'patience'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of rope used for hanging, so it is what someone would hang on.

clue.text: New Labour's turn to seek power in corruption

indicators.note: in tells us the power letter is placed inside the word for corruption

parts.note: sin means wickedness or corruption
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A political jibe about New Labour turning to seek power through corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: New Labour, the Blair-era British Labour Party, was notorious for its 'spin doctors' who put a favourable slant on news.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is a slanted presentation of news, the political turn most associated with New Labour's press operation.

clue.text: One or two points put over to strike out at in discourse

definitions.text: One or two points put over

indicators.note: to strike out means to cross something out of the following word

parts.note: conversation means discourse or talk

explanation.surface: A rugby or football commentary about kicking points and striking out in talk.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a conversion kicked over the posts is worth two points; in American football a conversion is worth one or two.
explanation.definitionFit: A successful kick or play after a try or touchdown, scoring one or two points, is called by this name.

clue.text: Students on this, we are affected?

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected or mannered
us is the object form of we

explanation.surface: Students asking whether they are pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a university, where students live and study.

clue.text: Haircuts set without middle layer always solid

parts.note: a perm is a curled hairstyle
an afro is a rounded, bushy hairstyle

indicators.note: without middle means the word set loses its central letter, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's set styled without the middle part, stiff as a board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haircuts' gives two styles, PERM and AFRO; 'set without middle' gives ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Permafrost is ground permanently frozen, a subsoil layer that stays solid all year.

clue.text: See 25
Might this treatment put the blame on your head?

definitions.text: Might this treatment put the blame on your head?

parts.note: rap means blame, as in taking the rap

indicators.note: your head means the first letter of the word your

explanation.surface: A wry question whether therapy just pins the blame on you.
explanation.walkthrough: THE, then RAP for blame, then the first letter of 'your'; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A course of treatment for psychological or physical problems, which might well make you face your own blame.

clue.text: 1 down entered in weak defence

indicators.note: entered in says the following pieces go inside the word for weak

parts.note: pale means feeble or weak, as in a pale imitation
the Roman numeral I is one
sad means down or unhappy

explanation.surface: A cross-reference saying 1 down was put into a feeble defence.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 down' looks like a reference to 1 down (WHIPLASH); it is I (one) and SAD (down).
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of pointed stakes built as a defence.

clue.text: Childhood affliction assuring attachment to mobile phone?

definitions.meaning: a condition of children where sticky fluid builds up in the middle ear
humorously, a substance sticking the phone permanently to one's ear

explanation.surface: A children's ailment imagined as the result of being glued to a phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue ear is a common childhood condition of fluid in the middle ear, and literally sticks something to the ear.

clue.text: Ace, by way of breaking into lofty pursuit

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
via means by way of

indicators.note: breaking signals the letters of into are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A star pilot breaking into the business of high flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking into' reads as forcing entry; 'breaking' is the anagram signal and INTO becomes TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviation is the activity of flying aircraft, a pursuit carried on high in the sky.

clue.text: Do penance for former head, one imprisoned

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: imprisoned says the letter for one is shut inside the word for head

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A former headmaster, now jailed, making amends.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a wrong is to atone or make amends for it, which is doing penance.

clue.text: Cricketer about to get left in peace, effect of changing viewpoint

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the word for peace

parts.note: pax is Latin for peace

indicators.note: about signals that the cricketer's name is turned round

parts.note: Brian Lara is the great West Indian batsman

explanation.surface: A cricketer coming back and being left alone in peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the batsman's name round; Brian Lara is a famous West Indian cricketer, and pax is Latin for peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallax is the apparent shift of an object's position when the observer's viewpoint changes.

clue.text: A non-U low-down location — it is a depressed area

indicators.note: non-U, a play on the British term for unrefined usage, here says the letter U is removed

parts.note: the rump is the bottom, a location low down on the body

explanation.surface: A remark that a vulgar, lowly place is a deprived area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' is British slang for not upper-class; here it means take U out of RUMP to leave RMP.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is a hollow under the arm, literally a depressed area of the body, and slang for a dismal place.

clue.text: Creator of elephants with elongated legs admitting height a bloomer

indicators.note: admitting says the height letter is let inside the painter's name

parts.words: Creator of elephants with elongated legs
parts.note: Salvador Dali painted elephants on spindly stilt-like legs

explanation.surface: A surreal artist's long-legged elephants making room for something tall, a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flower, i.e. something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A dahlia is a garden plant prized for its large flowers, so it is a bloomer.

clue.text: Local heading off to cut European flower

indicators.note: to cut says the trimmed word slices into the word for European

parts.note: a Dane is a native of Denmark, a European

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: the local is British slang for one's nearest pub

explanation.surface: A local man beheading a European flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows: a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as 'flow-er', a flower is something that flows, and the Danube is one of Europe's great rivers.

clue.text: Paul's to continue without a single idea

parts.note: the setter is Paul, so Paul's means Paul is, or I'm

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the second phrase wraps around the letter for one

parts.note: press on means to continue
a single is one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: The setter declaring he will carry on alone without a thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense 'outside', so the phrase for continue wraps round the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An impression is a vague notion or idea, as in 'I had the impression'.

clue.text: Cheese some cat effectively knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over means the letters are turned round
some says only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A cat efficiently tipping over some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ATEF lies within 'cAT EFfectively'; 'knocked over' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white Greek cheese made from sheep's or goat's milk.

clue.text: Don't eat so quickly

definitions.meaning: to go without food, as for a religious observance

explanation.surface: A parent telling a child to slow down at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to abstain from food, and fast also means rapidly.

clue.text: Bust width suited obedient wife, or abandonment? Eventually the latter, according to Mae West

definitions.text: Eventually the latter, according to Mae West

indicators.note: abandonment suggests letters thrown off all order, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tale of a buxom dutiful wife tempted by abandon, quoting Mae West.
explanation.walkthrough: Mae West's famous quip was 'I used to be Snow White, but I drifted'; Snow White is the pure obedient wife, drifting is abandonment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mae West's quip says she started pure, like Snow White, but ended up in abandon, the latter of the two options.
